Generate a small riverside ferry landing at dawn.
CAMERA: wide shot, camera at standing eye level on the gravel path behind the landing, looking across the jetty toward the water, the jetty read slightly at an angle, not square-on.
THE DOMINANT ELEMENT: pale dawn light rising from screen LEFT over the far bank, the willow side.
SPATIAL GEOGRAPHY (as seen from the path):
At the CENTRE, a short wooden jetty with grey weathered planks runs out over flat water. At the LEFT, a leaning willow tree with its branches touching the surface. At the RIGHT, a small tin ticket hut with a closed shutter. In the foreground, wet gravel and a coil of rope on a post.
Nothing else: no boats, no people, no other people, no animals, no modern signage, no phones.
Empty quiet landing, still air, light mist on the water.
Palette of roughly 75% grey-blue water and mist — 20% weathered wood brown — 5% pale gold sky.
Real material truth: split grey planks with rusted nail heads, rippled tin with flaking paint, wet gravel.
Dawn light from screen LEFT, the willow side, is the only key; the hut's bulb is off.
Image finish: ARRI Alexa Mini, 35mm lens, Kodak Vision3 250D. Era lock: early spring, early 1990s, rural South Korea. Nothing more recent anywhere in frame. No legible text anywhere.
